subject: Islamic Religious Studies
sourceFile: Copy of IRS BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: Based on the NERDC 2018 Islamic Studies curriculum for JSS 1-3, the exam assesses candidates' understanding of Islamic education based on the teachings of al-Qur'an and the Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (SAW), the responsibilities of a Muslim in applying Islamic principles in daily life, and lessons from Islam's historical and modern growth, across al-Qur'an, Hadith, Fiqh, Tawhid, Sirah and Tahdhib. There are two compulsory papers of 60 multiple-choice questions each, 1 hour each, one mark per question; the 120 questions make up 70% and the school's Continuous Assessment 30%. Paper 1 covers al-Qur'an, Fiqh and Tawhid; Paper 2 covers Hadith (24 questions), Sirah (24 questions) and Tahdhib (12 questions).
excluded: syllabus.ng 'About us', 'About BECE', eligibility, grading, registration and FAQ chapters (the FAQ is a copy of the History one). The Paper 1 breakdown in the source is copied from the History syllabus ('Concept of History', 'Geography and Environment') and was not used; Paper 1's coverage is inferred only from the syllabus tables. Topic numbering in the source skips XVII-XXI in the Qur'an section and mislabels the Beautiful Names sets ((I), (II), (III), (VI), unnumbered); they are numbered I-V here. Surah, Hadith and name transliterations were normalised from garbled extraction (e.g. 'Stiratul Fil', 'Madith', 'Al Muhsin' → 'Al-Muhsi', 'Al Muqaddir-The Expediter' → 'Al-Muqaddim', 'Invisibel' → 'Indivisible'); no Qur'anic or Hadith text was added.

Islamic Studies for Junior Secondary Schools — J.M. Kaura, D.A. Amoo, A.D. Muhammad, N.M. Hassan (University Press PLC, Ibadan)
Islamic Studies for Junior Secondary Schools Book 1-3 — Muhammad Bashir Sambo, Muhammad A. Higab, revised by Muktar Umar (Ahmadu Bello University Press Limited, Zaria)

topics.name: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) I
objectives: Read and give the meaning of the attributes of Allah as contained in Qur'an 59:23
State the significance of the attributes of Allah as contained in Qur'an 59:23
topics.content: Theme: Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). Attributes: Ar-Rahman (The Beneficent), Ar-Rahim (The Merciful), Al-Malik (The King), Al-Quddus (The Most Holy), As-Salam (The Source of Peace), Al-Mu'min (The Guardian of Faith).

topics.name: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) II
objectives: Read and give the meaning of the attributes of Allah as contained in Qur'an 59:24
State the significance of the attributes of Allah as contained in Qur'an 59:24
topics.content: Theme: Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). Attributes: Al-Muhaimin (The Protector), Al-Aziz (The All Mighty), Al-Jabbar (The Compeller), Al-Mutakabbir (The Dominant One), Al-Khaliq (The Creator), Al-Bari (The Maker), Al-Musawwir (The Flawless Shaper).

topics.name: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) III
objectives: Read and give the meaning of the attributes of Allah
State the significance of the attributes of Allah
topics.content: Theme: Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). Attributes: Al-Qadir (The All Capable; The Most Able), Al-Muqtadir (The All Determiner; The Dominant), Al-Muqaddim (The Expediter), Al-Mu'akhkhir (The Delayer), Al-Awwal (The First), Al-Akhir (The Last), Az-Zahir (The Manifest; The All Victorious), Al-Batin (The Hidden; The All Encompassing), Al-Wali (The Patron), Al-Muta'ali (The Self Exalted), Al-Barr (The Most Kind), At-Tawwab (The Ever-Pardoning), Al-Muntaqim (The Avenger), Al-'Afuww (The Forgiver), Ar-Ra'uf (The Clement; The Compassionate), Malikul Mulk (The Owner of All Sovereignty).

topics.name: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) IV
objectives: Read and give the meaning of the attributes of Allah
State the significance of the attributes of Allah
topics.content: Theme: Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). Attributes: Al-Ba'ith (The Raiser of the Dead), Ash-Shahid (The Witness of all), Al-Haqq (The Truth, The Real), Al-Wakil (The Trustee; The Dependable), Al-Qawiyy (The Strong), Al-Matin (The Firm; Steadfast), Al-Waliyy (The Patron; Supporter), Al-Hamid (The All Praiseworthy), Al-Muhsi (The Accounter of all), Al-Mubdi (The Originator and Initiator of all), Al-Mu'id (The Reinstater), Al-Muhyi (The Giver of Life), Al-Mumit (The Bringer of Death), Al-Hayy (The Ever Living), Al-Qayyum (The Self Subsisting, Sustainer of all), Al-Wajid (The Perceiver; Finder), Al-Wahid (The One, The All Inclusive), Al-Ahad (The One, the Indivisible), As-Samad (The Everlasting).

topics.name: The Beautiful Names of Allah (Asma'ul Husna) V
objectives: Read and give the meaning of the attributes of Allah
State the significance of the attributes of Allah
topics.content: Theme: Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). Attributes: Dhul Jalali wal Ikram (The Lord of Majesty and Generosity), Al-Jami (The Gatherer), Al-Ghaniyy (The All Rich; The Independent), Al-Mughni (The Enricher; The Emancipator), Al-Mani (The Withholder; The Shielder; The Defender), Ad-Darr (The Distresser), An-Nafi (The Benefactor), An-Nur (The Light), Al-Hadi (The Guide), Al-Badi (The Incomparable, The Originator), Al-Baqi (The Ever Enduring), Al-Warith (The Inheritor of all), Ar-Rashid (The Guide), As-Sabur (The Forbearing, The Patient).
